episodes.167755: A warm and rather humid air mass across central Indiana, combined with an approaching cold front in the afternoon to produce a line of strong to severe thunderstorms.  Wind damage was focused over the region's south-central counties;  the line also spawned two brief EF0 tornadoes before a longer track EF1 lifted and touched down several times across southern Shelby County.  A forth and final EF1 tornado tracked briefly over far southwestern Shelby County.
episodes.167761: A warm, moist airmass was in place across the region. As daytime heating interacted with a passing disturbance in the atmosphere, showers and storms developed during the late afternoon. Thanks to cold temperatures aloft, some of these storms were able to reach strong to severe limits with hail being prevalent and some storms also produced wind damage in the form of blowing down a few trees. These storms diminished through the evening hours.
episodes.167763: A mid level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass across Vermont during the late afternoon/early evening of May 21st. Scattered thunderstorms developed in NY and southern Quebec and intensified as they moved east into VT. Several reports of damaging winds and a few observations of hail greater than one inch in diameter were reported.
episodes.167768: A mid level disturbance moved into a moderately unstable airmass across southern Ontario/southern Quebec and northern NY during the late afternoon/early evening of May 21st. Scattered thunderstorms in southern Ontario/Quebec intensified as they moved along the international border and began to develop southward. Isolated hail and strong winds were reported along the international border.
episodes.167828: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across east-central Florida as the east coast sea breeze moved inland from the coast, and eventually collided with the west coast sea breeze. Many storms became severe and produced quarter to half dollar sized hail over parts of Seminole, Volusia, and Lake Counties. Another severe thunderstorm in Lake County produced straight-line wind damage in Tavares.
episodes.167837: A low pressure system approached the area on May 21st, which allowed for the development of a few showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening across the Ohio Valley. A few stronger storms developed along eastern West Virginia, one of which was strong enough to produce damaging winds which caused the roof of a gas station to collapse in Wyoming County.
episodes.167868: Isolated to scattered pulse type convection occurred during the afternoon into the early evening hours. One storm became severe and produced significant wind damage north of the Anderson and east of Lexington in Lauderdale county.
episodes.167921: A low pressure system approached the area on May 21st, which allowed for the development of a few showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening across the Ohio Valley. A stronger storm moved through northeast Kentucky which produced damaging winds and caused several trees to be blown down in Carter County.
episodes.168042: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in an unstable air mass in place across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.168044: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in an unstable air mass in place across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.168113: Scattered storms developed in the mountains and foothills of northeast Tennessee in the afternoon. A few of the storms produced large hail to the size of quarters as they tracked northeast.
episodes.168257: Excessive rain in the James basin resulted in the river at Ashton entering flood stage on May 20th, and at the end of the month the peak stage was 16.56 feet. At this level, impacts are primarily limited to flooded agricultural lands.
episodes.168277: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developing on the afternoon of May 21st in a moderate to strongly unstable environment with MLCAPE values in excess of 2000 J/kg but relatively weak shear. Atmospheric moisture was high with precipitable water values greater than 1.5 inches. Storms that developed were slow moving and trained over the same area around Columbia causing significant flooding in downtown including the Five Points area and at the intersection of Main and Whaley St.
episodes.168331: A cluster of thunderstorms over parts of southern Illinois intensified as it moved into an increasingly unstable air mass as temperatures warmed to near 80. Gradually strengthening southwesterly winds in the low and mid levels of the atmosphere aided in the formation of an organized line. The line of storms posed a gradually increasing threat for damaging winds as it encountered a more unstable air mass. The storms formed in the vicinity of a cold front as it sagged southeast toward western Indiana, southern Illinois, and south central Missouri.
episodes.168332: A cluster of thunderstorms over parts of southern Illinois intensified as it moved into an  increasingly unstable air mass over Indiana as temperatures warmed into the 80's. Gradually strengthening southwesterly winds in the low and mid levels of the atmosphere aided in the organization of a line of storms. The line of storms posed a gradually increasing threat for damaging winds as it encountered a more unstable air mass. Small bowing clusters of storms produced several damaging wind gusts over southwest Indiana.  The storms formed in the vicinity of a cold front as it sagged southeast toward western Indiana, southern Illinois, and south central Missouri.
episodes.168333: Thunderstorms intensified on the southern periphery of a thunderstorm complex moving across southern Illinois. These storms were just to the cool side of an outflow boundary sagging southeast from the Illinois storms. Solar heating and destabilization resulted in enough of an increase in the storms for isolated large hail.
episodes.168334: Thunderstorms intensified on the southern periphery of a thunderstorm complex moving across southern Illinois. These storms were just to the cool side of an outflow boundary sagging south from the Illinois storms. Solar heating and destabilization resulted in enough of an increase in the storms for isolated strong wind gusts.
episodes.168674: A small cluster of vigorous convective cells developed along an outflow boundary moving north across the Straits of Florida from earlier strong thunderstorms over Cuba.  A small area of gale-force wind gusts occurred in the coastal waters near Marathon.
episodes.168751: On the morning of the 21st, a cold front was located just west and north of Lake Erie, across southeastern Lower MI and southern ON. This front drifted southeastward to near the major axis of Lake Erie by early evening and then moved little through the wee hours of the 22nd. The front encountered primarily moderate to strong and elevated MUCAPE, and moderate to strong effective bulk shear over and near the lake. Two separate lines of multicellular thunderstorms occurred along and in vicinity of the front during the late morning and early evening. Some of these storms generated gale-force peak wind gusts.
episodes.168755: On the morning of the 21st, a cold front extended southwestward from southern ON to far-northwestern OH. This front drifted southeastward through the early evening, when it became located in vicinity of the major axis of Lake Erie, west-central OH, and east-central IN. The front then moved little through the wee hours of the 22nd. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms occurred along and ahead of the front during the afternoon through early evening. Some of these storms produced severe hail and damaging wind gusts. In particular, a supercell managed to produce hail as large as golf balls to two-inches in diameter in Geauga County. The ambient environment consisted of moderate to strong effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.168803: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front pushed through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind, and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168804: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front moved through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind, and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168806: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front moved through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168856: During the morning and afternoon hours of May 21st, the advection of warmth and moisture into the Upper Ohio Valley helped to build daytime instability.  A couple of thunderstorm lines developed ahead of an evening cold front. In an environment of sufficient shear, many reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.168894: An upper level storm system pushing north into the foothills and Piedmont of North Carolina helped trigger a few severe thunderstorms.
episodes.168900: An upper level storm system lifting north into southern Virginia helped trigger scattered thunderstorms. A few of these storms became severe with localized damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.169020: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in summerlike conditions during the early evening hours. The thunderstorms produced a couple reports of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169021: A cluster of strong thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast near the Altamaha River. These thunderstorms then moved out across the Atlantic coastal waters and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.169034: An increase in deep moisture with PWAT values nearing 1.8 inches increased convective coverage of sea breeze induced showers and storms over an unstable airmass with steeper mid level lapse rates.
episodes.169050: Strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in small hail and some wind damage across portions of northeast SC.
episodes.169091: An increase in deep moisture with PWAT values nearing 1.8 inches increased convective coverage of sea breeze induced showers and storms over an unstable airmass with steeper mid level lapse rates.
episodes.169208: Minor flooding of the White River inundated some low-lying fields, including cropland. Several rounds of rain and thunderstorms on May 19th and again on May 21st brought heavy rainfall to southern Indiana. Lower portions of the White River rose above flood stage for a few days.
episodes.169364: A weak cold front moved into a moist and unstable airmass, resulting in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, a few of which were severe.
episodes.169374: A cold front brought a round of strong thunderstorms to the area with a few gusts measured in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.169386: A cold front set up just west of Kentucky and became stalled throughout the day on May 21. Ahead of this cold front, Kentucky was experiencing warm, humid, and unstable conditions across the region. By the afternoon, this led to the development of multiple lines of showers and thunderstorms. The general trend was for these storms to begin dissipating the farther east they went, out of the most unstable air. Best instability, along with the most potent line of storms, were located to our west across western and central Kentucky, nearer to the frontal boundary. However, this didn't deter an individual storm from continuing ahead of the main line and impacting Rowan and Fleming Counties, resulting in some wind damage in Rowan County as it moved through.
episodes.169436: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues.  Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.
episodes.169438: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues. Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.
episodes.169466: During the morning and afternoon hours of May 21st, the advection of warmth and moisture into the Upper Ohio Valley helped to build daytime instability.  A couple of thunderstorm lines developed ahead of an evening cold front. Only a couple of wind damage reports and a single hail report were received, as thunderstorms became stronger and more numerous after crossing into Pennsylvania.
episodes.169510: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues. Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.
episodes.169564: Trees were reported down near New Baltimore.
episodes.169565: A thunderstorm moving through the Detroit River produced a wind gust near 45 knots.
episodes.169566: A thunderstorm moving through western Lake Erie produced a wind gust near 45 knots.
episodes.169588: Strong thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 21st, along and behind a slowly advancing cold front. The strongest storms produced hail.
episodes.169625: A slow moving cold front triggered showers and thunderstorms across the region from the late evening of the 20th to the late afternoon of the 21st. A few of the stronger storms produced wind gusts over 60 mph and hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter. There were also several reports of flooding along the Interstate 44 corridor. Rainfall accumulations averaged between one half inch and one inch, with isolated accumulations over 2.5 inches near Fort Leonard Wood and Rolla.
episodes.169693: A broad upper level trough brought a cold front to South Central Texas and into a warm, moist airmass. Thunderstorms developed along the front and some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.169758: As a cold front moved through storms developed. A couple of the storms became severe.
episodes.169759: A line of storms moved through southern Illinois. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.169760: Storms moved through the region during the afternoon and evening of May 21st. One storm produced large hail.
episodes.169772: A weak shortwave trough in the southwest flow at mid-levels initiated showers and thunderstorms over Georgia and South Carolina during the early afternoon hours.  These storms propagated into the southern and western Piedmont of central North Carolina by mid-afternoon, while additional storms developed into the central Piedmont and Coastal Plain and moved north toward Virginia during the evening hours. Many of the storms produced small hail and damaging winds, while a few storms produced one inch hail.
episodes.169875: Both a morning round and afternoon round of isolated severe thunderstorms occurred. Two lightning strikes caused fires as well. Trees and outbuildings were damaged from severe thunderstorm winds, and semi trucks were blown over.
episodes.169885: Thunderstorms on the afternoon of May 21 downed trees, branches, and produced small hail in Allen county, Ohio.
episodes.169977: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced large hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169980: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over the South Carolina piedmont during the afternoon. One of the storms produced large hail in York County.
episodes.170014: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced baseball size hail at Fort Griffin in Shackleford County. Also, there were a few more hail reports from isolated strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.170044: An upper level ridge was centered over Florida on the 21st of May. A shortwave trough moving northward on the western periphery of that ridge passed right over the local area, providing enough upper level support to support a few severe thunderstorms over the coastal waters. One offshore site was hit by multiple storms, one right after the other.
episodes.170095: The air mass on Saturday, May 21st, was becoming increasingly unstable in advance of a approaching cold front.  Modified morning soundings indicated a very unstable air mass by the afternoon. Surface based CAPE was in the 4000-4500 J/kg with enough dry air aloft for damaging downburst winds.  The severe threat would emerge again on Sunday as the cold front moved through Alabama.
episodes.170097: An upper-level trough and surface cold front approached central Kentucky from the west during the day on May 21st. Ahead of the front, warm temperatures and a moist atmosphere contributed to a highly unstable environment. There were two main rounds of convection which produced severe weather with this event. Multicell clusters developed out ahead of the front during the early afternoon hours, producing hail and wind damage across the Kentucky Bluegrass. Then, a broken line of convection associated with the front itself caused some wind damage across the Louisville metro.
episodes.170112: Scattered strong to severe storms formed into a line across portions of northwestern and northern Arkansas along and ahead of an advancing cold front. The line made it into central sections of the state by early evening, and into the south during the overnight hours of the 21st.||Dry weather and above normal temperatures returned to the state for a few days before yet another storm system would impact the state on the 21st. Ahead of a strong cold front, there was a risk of severe weather stretching from the Texas/Mexico border northeastward to the Maine/Canada border. Thunderstorms initially developed across north/northwest Arkansas before forming into a line and marching east. While a brief, weak tornado occurred across Newton County, the most widespread damage occurred across portions of north central into northeast Arkansas. Numerous trees were blown down from Sharp County into portions of Lawrence and Randolph Counties. Additional storms developed later during the evening of May 21st across portions of western into central and southern Arkansas. Severe weather reports weren't widespread, but a second brief tornado developed near Royal in Garland County.
episodes.170143: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of south central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.170284: On May 21st, thunderstorms developed along a combination of a dryline and cold front across the southwestern portions of the region. These storms merged into an eastward moving complex of storms that produced strong winds across some of our Central Texas counties. On May 24th, numerous showers and storms affected the area due primarily to a series of boundaries and shortwaves. A complex of storms moved across parts of Central Texas but was weakening, and only one report of severe criteria winds was reported.
episodes.170422: An upper-level trough and surface cold front approached southern Indiana from the west during the day on May 21st. Ahead of the front, warm temperatures and a moist atmosphere contributed to a highly unstable environment. A broken line of convection associated with the front caused wind damage across four southern Indiana counties.
episodes.170448: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior mountains.  A pre-frontal trough ahead of an approaching cold front triggered a long line of severe thunderstorms that had a history of causing wind damage across Quebec province.  This line of storms reached the Maine border during the evening on May 21st.
episodes.170450: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior mountains. A pre-frontal trough ahead of an approaching cold front triggered a long line of severe thunderstorms that had a history of causing wind damage across Quebec province. This line of storms reached the New Hampshire border during the evening on May 21st.
episodes.170496: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected parts of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on May 21, producing a few reports of large hail and wind damage.
